title: Little words, big meaning: particles and invitations
objectives: Use the enclitic particles na, pa, lang, din/rin, daw/raw, and naman
Place particles correctly in second position
Make plans with balak and gusto + linker + verb
Invite someone out, accept warmly, and decline politely

grammar.title: Na, pa, lang: already, still, just
grammar.explanation:
Tagalog carries a set of tiny particles that never start a sentence; they cling to the first word (or first word plus pronoun). These 'enclitics' carry a huge amount of everyday meaning.

NA = already / now: 'Kumain na ako' — I've already eaten. 'Tara na!' — Let's go now! 'Malaki na siya' — he's big now (he's grown).

PA = still / yet / more: 'Kumakain pa ako' — I'm still eating. With negatives: 'Hindi pa ako kumain' — I haven't eaten yet. 'Wala pa siya' — she's not here yet. Also 'more': 'Isa pa!' — one more!

LANG = just / only: 'Dalawa lang kami' — there are just two of us. 'Nagbibiro lang ako' — I'm just joking. You met it with the kaka- form: 'Kakauwi ko lang.'

Na and pa are mirror twins, and answering questions with them is a core skill: 'Kumain ka na ba?' — 'Oo, kumain na ako.' / 'Hindi pa.'

examples.tl: Tapos ka na ba? — Hindi pa. Konti na lang!
examples.en: Are you done? — Not yet. Just a little more!
Let's leave now. It's already late (night).

examples.tl: May kanin pa ba? — Wala na.
examples.en: Is there still rice? — There's none left.

examples.tl: Isang tanong lang, tapos aalis na ako.
examples.en: Just one question, then I'll go.

grammar.title: Din/rin, daw/raw, naman
grammar.explanation:
DIN/RIN = also/too. Use rin after a word ending in a vowel or w/y, din elsewhere: 'Ako rin!' — me too! 'Gutom din ako' — I'm hungry too. Manila speakers are relaxed about this rule, but rin-after-vowel is the classic pattern.

DAW/RAW = reportedly, '(someone) said'. Same sound rule: raw after vowels. It marks second-hand information: 'Uulan daw bukas' — they say it'll rain tomorrow. 'Darating raw sila nang alas-siyete' — they said they'll arrive at seven. It saves you a whole 'he said that...' clause.

NAMAN is the hardest to translate and the most Filipino of all. Its core jobs at this level: (1) mild contrast or turn-taking — 'Ako naman' — my turn / as for me; 'Ikaw naman?' — and you? (2) softening — 'Okay naman' — it's okay (really); 'Hindi naman' — not really. Don't agonize over a perfect translation; collect examples and copy them.

Order matters when particles stack: short pronouns come before particles ('Kumain na ako' → with two: 'Kumain na rin ako' — I ate too, finally), and na/pa come before other particles: na rin, pa lang, na naman (again!).

examples.tl: Masarap daw ang pagkain sa bagong restawran.
examples.en: They say the food at the new restaurant is delicious.

examples.tl: Kumusta ka? — Okay naman. Ikaw naman, kumusta?
examples.en: How are you? — I'm fine. And you, how are you?

grammar.title: Balak and gusto + verb: plans and invitations
grammar.explanation:
In A1 you used gusto with nouns: 'Gusto ko ng kape.' To want TO DO something, keep the ng-form actor and add the linker to it, then the basic verb: 'Gusto kong kumain' — I want to eat. 'Gusto mo bang sumama?' — Do you want to come along? Balak (plan/intend) works exactly the same way: 'Balak kong pumunta sa Baguio sa Disyembre' — I plan to go to Baguio in December.

To invite someone, the friendliest openers are: 'Gusto mo bang manood ng sine?' (Want to watch a movie?), 'Sama ka!' (Come with us!), and the beloved 'Tara!' / 'Tara na!' (Let's go!). Accept with 'Sige!' 'G!' (very casual), 'Oo naman!'

Declining needs softening — a flat 'Ayaw ko' sounds rude. The polite formula is sana (expressing a wish that won't happen) + a reason + a rain check: 'Gusto ko sana, kaso may lakad ako' — I'd love to, but I have plans. 'Sa susunod na lang, ha?' — Next time instead, okay? May lakad ako (literally 'I have a walk/errand') is the all-purpose Filipino excuse.

examples.tl: Gusto mo bang kumain sa labas mamayang gabi?
examples.en: Do you want to eat out tonight?

examples.tl: Balak naming magbakasyon sa La Union.
examples.en: We plan to take a vacation in La Union.

examples.tl: Gusto ko sana, kaso kailangan kong magtrabaho bukas.
examples.en: I'd love to, but I need to work tomorrow.

examples.tl: Sayang! Sa susunod na lang, ha?
examples.en: Too bad! Next time then, okay?

example.tl: Tapos na ang klase.
example.en: The class is already over.

example.tl: Nag-aaral pa siya sa kolehiyo.
example.en: She's still studying in college.

example.tl: Biro lang!
example.en: Just kidding!

vocab.note: rin after vowels, din after consonants

example.tl: Gusto ko rin ng halo-halo.
example.en: I want halo-halo too.

example.tl: May party daw sa Sabado.
example.en: They say there's a party on Saturday.

example.tl: Ako naman ang magluluto ngayon.
example.en: This time I'll be the one to cook.

vocab.note: gusto ko sana = I'd love to (but...)

example.tl: Sana pumayag ang nanay mo.
example.en: Hopefully your mom agrees.

example.tl: Gusto ko sana, kaso wala akong pera.
example.en: I'd love to, but I have no money.

vocab.note: balak kong + verb = I plan to

example.tl: Ano ang balak mo sa Sabado?
example.en: What's your plan for Saturday?

example.tl: May plano ba kayo mamayang gabi?
example.en: Do you have plans tonight?

vocab.note: may lakad ako = I have plans (common excuse)

example.tl: May lakad kami ng pamilya ko bukas.
example.en: My family and I have plans tomorrow.

vocab.note: sumama, sumasama, sasama; Sama ka! = come with us!

example.tl: Gusto mo bang sumama sa amin?
example.en: Do you want to come with us?

vocab.note: irregular mang- verb, learn as-is: nanood, nanonood, manonood

example.tl: Nanood kami ng sine kagabi.
example.en: We watched a movie last night.

example.tl: Magkita tayo sa mall nang alas-kuwatro.
example.en: Let's meet at the mall at four.

example.tl: Mag-usap tayo mamaya, ha?
example.en: Let's talk later, okay?

example.tl: Magbabakasyon kami sa Palawan.
example.en: We're going on vacation in Palawan.

vocab.note: manood ng sine = watch a movie

example.tl: Ano ang maganda sa sine ngayon?
example.en: What's good at the movies right now?

example.tl: May konsyerto raw sa Sabado sa arena.
example.en: They say there's a concert on Saturday at the arena.

vocab.note: from handa; a Filipino house party

example.tl: May handaan sa bahay nila sa Linggo.
example.en: There's a party at their house on Sunday.

example.tl: Pupunta kami sa kasal ng pinsan ko.
example.en: We're going to my cousin's wedding.

example.tl: Sumama ka na, libre ko ang kape mo.
example.en: Come along, my treat for coffee.

example.tl: Tara! Manood tayo ng sine!
example.en: Come on! Let's watch a movie!

example.tl: Sayang! Hindi ako puwede sa Sabado.
example.en: Too bad! I can't make it on Saturday.

vocab.note: sa susunod na lang = (let's do it) next time instead

example.tl: Sa susunod na lang tayo manood, ha?
example.en: Let's just watch next time, okay?

example.tl: Siguro darating sila nang alas-sais.
example.en: They'll probably arrive at six.

example.tl: Okupado ako buong linggo, e.
example.en: I'm busy all week, you see.

example.tl: Malapit na ang kaarawan ni Ana.
example.en: Ana's birthday is coming up.

dialogue.title: Movie night, maybe
dialogue.context: Officemates Bea and Jerome are chatting during their break on a Friday afternoon.

lines.speaker: Bea
lines.tl: Jerome! May bago raw na horror movie sa sine. Maganda raw talaga.
lines.en: Jerome! They say there's a new horror movie showing. It's supposed to be really good.

lines.speaker: Jerome
lines.tl: Ah, oo! Sabi rin ng kapatid ko. Nanood na siya.
lines.en: Oh, yes! My sibling said so too. He's already seen it.

lines.speaker: Bea
lines.tl: Gusto mo bang manood mamayang gabi? Sama na!
lines.en: Want to watch tonight? Come on, join!

lines.speaker: Jerome
lines.tl: Naku, gusto ko sana, kaso may lakad ako mamaya. May handaan sa bahay ng tita ko.
lines.en: Oh no, I'd love to, but I have plans later. There's a party at my aunt's house.

lines.speaker: Bea
lines.tl: Sayang naman! Sa Sabado na lang kaya?
lines.en: Too bad! How about Saturday instead?

lines.speaker: Jerome
lines.tl: Sa Sabado... puwede! Wala pa akong plano.
lines.en: Saturday... I can! I don't have plans yet.

lines.speaker: Bea
lines.tl: Ayos! Balak ko ring kumain sa bagong ramen place pagkatapos. Masarap daw doon.
lines.en: Great! I also plan to eat at the new ramen place afterwards. They say it's delicious there.

lines.speaker: Jerome
lines.tl: Sige! Gutom na ako, e. Anong oras tayo magkikita?
lines.en: Deal! I'm getting hungry already. What time will we meet?

lines.speaker: Bea
lines.tl: Alas-kuwatro siguro, sa labas ng mall. Maaga pa, puwede tayong mag-kape muna.
lines.en: Maybe four o'clock, outside the mall. It's still early, we can have coffee first.

lines.speaker: Jerome
lines.tl: Ikaw naman ang taya sa kape, ha? Libre ko na ang tiket.
lines.en: You're covering the coffee then, okay? The tickets are my treat.

lines.speaker: Bea
lines.tl: Sige, deal! Huwag kang male-late, ha?
lines.en: Okay, deal! Don't be late, okay?

lines.speaker: Jerome
lines.tl: Hindi naman ako laging late! Minsan lang.
lines.en: I'm not always late! Only sometimes.

exercises.explain: Na marks 'already/now': the eating is done. 'Still eating' would be kumakain pa ako.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks 'Kumain ka na ba?' and you haven't eaten. The natural answer is:
exercises.explain: Hindi pa = not yet. Pa pairs with negatives to mean the thing hasn't happened yet.
Din/rin means 'also'. After the consonant of 'Cebu'... actually Cebu ends in a vowel, so rin is the classic choice, but Manila speakers use both — we accept either.

exercises.prompt: What does daw/raw add to 'Uulan daw bukas'?
choices: The speaker heard it from someone else
exercises.explain: Daw/raw marks reported information: 'they say it will rain tomorrow.'

exercises.prompt: Kumusta ka? — Okay ___. Ikaw? (I'm fine, thanks — softened)
exercises.explain: Okay naman softens and rounds off the answer; naman also powers the return question 'Ikaw naman?'

exercises.prompt: Where does the particle go? 'I still study at the university' =
exercises.explain: Enclitic particles sit in second position, right after the first full word: nag-aaral pa ako. (Pa can never start a sentence.)

exercises.prompt: Gusto ___ bang sumama sa amin? (Do you want to come with us?)
exercises.explain: Gusto keeps its ng-form actor (mo) even with a verb; ba follows, then the linker feeds into sumama.

exercises.tl: Gusto ko sana, kaso may lakad ako bukas. Sa susunod na lang, ha?
choices: Declining politely and suggesting next time
exercises.explain: Gusto ko sana (I'd love to) + kaso + excuse (may lakad ako) + sa susunod na lang is the classic polite decline.

exercises.prompt: I plan to go to Baguio in December.
exercises.answer: Balak kong pumunta sa Baguio sa Disyembre.
accept: Balak kong pumunta sa Baguio sa Disyembre
Balak kong pumunta sa Disyembre sa Baguio
Sa Disyembre, balak kong pumunta sa Baguio
exercises.explain: Balak works like gusto: ng-form actor + linker (kong) + basic verb (pumunta).

exercises.prompt: 'Uulan na naman.' What does na naman express?
exercises.explain: The combination na naman means 'again', often with a sigh: here we go again.

exercises.prompt: Masarap daw ang pagkain doon, kaso wala akong pera ngayon.
exercises.answer: They say the food there is delicious, but I have no money right now.
accept: They say the food there is delicious, but I have no money right now
The food there is supposedly delicious but I don't have money right now
They say the food is delicious there, but I have no money now
exercises.explain: Daw marks hearsay; kaso introduces the casual 'but'; wala akong pera = I have no money.

exercises.prompt: Let's meet at the mall at four. Don't be late, okay?
exercises.answer: Magkita tayo sa mall nang alas-kuwatro. Huwag kang male-late, ha?
accept: Magkita tayo sa mall nang alas-kuwatro. Huwag kang male-late, ha
Magkita tayo sa mall nang alas-kwatro. Huwag kang male-late ha
Magkita tayo sa mall sa alas-kuwatro. Huwag kang male-late, ha
exercises.explain: Magkita tayo = let's meet (inclusive tayo); huwag + kang for the negative command, with the friendly tag ha.

exercises.prompt: Put the particles in the right order: 'I ate too, already.'
exercises.explain: When particles stack, na comes before rin, and both come before longer words but after the verb: kumain na rin ako.

exercises.prompt: ___! Manood tayo ng sine! (Come on! Let's watch a movie!)
exercises.explain: Tara (or Tara na) is the go-to friendly 'let's go / come on' for launching an invitation.
